correctness.rationale: The operator identity is equivalent to both image and kernel being Lie subalgebras (verified by substitution for an idempotent). Every complement has exactly one central subalgebra; noncentral factors are precisely graphs over totally isotropic subspaces. Counting isotropic frames modulo bases and vector-space complements yields the exact rank counts for all prime powers and m≥2. The explicit F factorization has a uniformly bounded product quotient and a quadratic exponent peaking at (8m+3)/10, proving the fixed-q concentration and equal-mixture limit. A self-contained checker independently confirms complete counts by subalgebra-pair enumeration at (m,q)=(1,2),(1,3),(2,2) and by exhaustive operator matrices at q=2,3, all successful. Finite checks are not claimed to prove infinite theorems.

value.rationale: The count is a complete natural higher-dimensional rank classification for idempotent Lie Rota–Baxter operators, a structural statistic arising from Lie algebra factorizations. The unexpected 4/5 low-factor dimension, symmetric rank branches 2/5 and 3/5, and bounded-width concentration explain the typical geometry of random complementary Lie subalgebras. Arbitrary m≥2, arbitrary q, and a sharp fixed-field limit move decisively beyond the known three-dimensional matrix classification and standard correspondence, rather than an isolated small enumeration.
